mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 0.5% indicates a dual signal of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which raises real discount rates and erodes purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both HOUST and GDPC1 signals weakening housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both decline in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which initially boosts consumer spending but eventually leads to higher wage pressures and inflation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in a low-inflation regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered low-inflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in INDPRO accompanied by a concurrent decline in RSAFS signals both supply contraction and reduced savings, which depresses corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and RSAFS both decline in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
